title: fix(cli): `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` refuses an `--out` it cannot write before executing anything
body:
Fixes #23826

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`os migrate organization-ownership --apply` wrote its report file only after the ceremony had executed and the stack had shut down (`writeFile(FILE, …, { flag: 'wx' })`), so an `--out` that could not be written was discovered last. The failure went through `refuse()`, whose `--json` code for every apply refusal is `apply_refused`, the code a refusal before any write prints.

Positive control, reproduced on the base `f7e836da1e` against a local SQLite fixture (a served boot of this tree, `organization_id` added to `sys_migration_journal`; the plan run, then `--apply --backup-taken --plan-file PLAN --out EXISTING --json`):

- payload `{"error":"apply_refused","reason":"report-file-unwritable","file":"…/apply.json","detail":"EEXIST: file already exists, open '…/apply.json'"}`, exit 1;
- yet the ceremony had executed: the `sys_migration` marker row `adr-0131-organization-ownership` present, `sys_migration_journal.organization_id` dropped (the existing file itself was untouched).

## What changes

All in `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`: the apply run's `--out` handling, plus one branch in `refuse()`'s code selection.

1. **The report file is reserved before the apply boots**, after the plan-file and backup preconditions. The reservation is an exclusive create (`open(FILE, 'wx')`), not an existence check, so no concurrent creator can take the path between the check and the write. It runs before `bootSchemaStack`, so it holds under either boot posture, including `deferredDdlUnsupported: 'skip-schema-sync'` on a Turso remote primary. An `--out` that cannot be created is refused at that point with `apply_refused`, `reason: report-file-unwritable`, `file` and the OS `code` (`EEXIST`, `ENOENT`, `EACCES`, …). Nothing is executed.
2. **The reserved file says what it is.** Until the report is written over it, it holds a short JSON note: `"kind": "organization-ownership-apply-reservation"`, `reservedAt`, and one sentence naming the ledger row and the re-run. A run with nothing to report (a refusal after the boot, a failed step, a boot failure) removes it, so a resume can reuse the path. A run killed before its report leaves the note, never an empty file.
3. **A report lost after the ceremony executed gets its own code.** The report is written through the reserved file's handle. It may still fail to be kept there: a write error, or the path no longer names the reserved file because it was removed or replaced while the run went on. The payload is then `{"error":"apply_report_unwritable","reason":"report-write-failed","file","detail","executed":true,"report":{…}}`, exit 1, with the full report. A write error adds its OS `code`. A path that no longer names the reserved file adds `standing` (`removed` or `replaced`) and no `code`: that is not an OS error, so no errno code is invented for it. The text output keeps "The ceremony ran" and says whether every step finished. A path that was replaced is never written to or removed.
4. **The default name** (no `--out`) is now stamped when the file is reserved, before the boot. It used to come from `report.generatedAt`, which exists only after the ceremony.

**New JSON `error` value: `apply_report_unwritable`.** I grepped `packages/cli/src`, `content/docs` and `docs/` for readers of the existing four values (`apply_refused`, `plan_refused`, `boot_failed`, `apply_failed`). Nothing reads them outside this command and its tests. Sibling commands print a `boot_failed` of their own. No doc names any of the four, so no doc needed an update. The changeset names the new value.

## The dispatch's mechanism assumptions, measured

1. **Held on `f7e836da1e`.** The apply boot is at `:516`-`:531`, `stack.shutdown()` is in `finally` at `:734`, and the `wx` write is at `:739`. Its refusal goes through `refuse()` (`:240`-`:252`) as `apply_refused`. Reproduced above.
2. **The default path.** Without `--out`, the old default name embedded `report.generatedAt`, so a collision there was not the measured shape. An unwritable current directory still was: a read-only filesystem, no write permission as a non-root user, or a removed working directory. Each executed the ceremony first. The default path is now reserved the same way, so each of those refuses before the boot too.
3. **What the reserved file holds in each outcome:**
   - refused after the boot (here, a plan that is not the reviewed one): removed (integration pin iii);
   - boot failure: removed (unit pin);
   - completed: the report;
   - lost after execution: nothing at the path, and the report in the payload (integration pin iv);
   - killed: the note. The unit pins read the note at the boot, the first point after the reservation where a run can be cut off. A kill between the `open` and the note's single write would leave an empty file; that window is one write call.

## Tests

- `organization-ownership.report-file.integration.test.ts` (integration tier: a served boot builds the fixture, then the real command runs the plan and `--apply`):
  - (i) existing `--out`: `apply_refused` / `report-file-unwritable` / `code: EEXIST` / `file`, exit 1; no marker row; the column the ceremony drops still present; the existing file byte-identical.
  - (ii) control, new `--out`: the ceremony executes (marker present, column dropped) and the report is written there.
  - (iii) refused after the boot (digest mismatch): the reservation note is on disk at the boot and gone afterwards; no marker row.
  - (iv) the reserved file removed after the boot: `apply_report_unwritable` / `report-write-failed` / `standing: removed` / no `code` / `executed: true` plus `report.steps`, exit 1; the ceremony executed (marker present, column dropped).
- `organization-ownership.report-reservation.test.ts` (unit tier, boot stubbed to fail):
  - existing `--out`: refused before the boot (`EEXIST`), file untouched;
  - missing directory: refused before the boot (`ENOENT`);
  - control: a new `--out` holds the reservation note at the boot and is released afterwards;
  - no `--out`: the default name is reserved in the working directory at the boot and released afterwards.

### Results at `81a98be381` (the head this PR opens with; every run on a shared box)

Patch round 1 moved the head to `d58cb29ddd`: a lost reservation now carries `standing`, not an invented errno `code` (case (iv) above). Its re-runs are in the `os-dev-report` on #23826, and CI on that head is green.

- **New pins.** `organization-ownership.report-file.integration.test.ts`: 4/4 pass. `organization-ownership.report-reservation.test.ts`: 4/4 pass. `organization-ownership.apply-flags.test.ts`: 7/7 pass.
- **Negative control (ablation).** Run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, with a restore trap.
  - Mutation: `open(file, 'wx')` became `open(file, 'w')` in the reservation. The anchor went 1 to 0, and the blob went from `659b66145cf5` to `368b06a9329a`.
  - Effect: exactly the two existing-`--out` pins went red. The unit pin received `boot_failed` (the boot was reached). Integration pin (i) received the success payload `{file, report}`: the ceremony executed and overwrote the file. The other 6 cases stayed green.
  - Restore proven: the blob is back at the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
  - The subject resolves from `src/` (a relative import inside the package), so no `dist/` rebuild was involved.
- **CLI unit project (`--project unit`).** 300 of 302 files and 4482 of 4485 tests passed. The 3 failures were 5-second timeouts on a loaded box, in `src/utils/boot-preparation-parity.test.ts` and `test/hook-timeout-override-refusal.test.ts`. Neither file reads this command. Rerun alone, both pass: 45/45 together with the new unit file.
- **Every integration file that drives this ceremony.** 14 files: 13 pass; 159 tests pass. The 14th, `organization-ownership.remote-face.integration.test.ts` (a Turso remote primary over `sqld`), skips itself here because this container has no `sqld` binary. That leaves the remote posture unmeasured locally; the reservation runs before the boot, so it does not depend on the posture. The rest of the integration tier is left to CI's `Test Core`.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`** exits 0. That covers `tsc --noEmit`, whose program includes both new test files, and `check:test-typecheck`.
- **`pnpm exec eslint`** on the three changed source and test files exits 0.
- **Derived gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 65 families. All 65 exit 0, and `--ran` reconciles 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. Four of them (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:i18n-walk-parity`) first exited 3, a missing prerequisite (the CLI's own `dist/`). They were rerun green after a cached `turbo` build of the CLI and the packages those gates name.

## Acceptance notes

- **Plan path (hold-off, unchanged).** The plan path (`:396`-`:410` on the base) still writes its `--out` after the read-only plan run. That run changes nothing in the database, so an existing plan `--out` costs only the wasted plan run (`plan_refused` / `plan-file-unwritable`).
- **Text mode.** Without `--json`, a report lost after execution is not printed. The message names the re-run with a new `--out`, which resumes and writes the report. `--json` carries the full report in the payload.
- **Existing unit case.** The case "with --backup-taken, goes on to the boot" in `organization-ownership.apply-flags.test.ts` passes no `--out`. Its run now creates a reservation file in vitest's working directory (the package directory) and removes it again around its stubbed boot failure.
- **No merge with main.** I did not merge `origin/main` before opening. The commits since the base touch spec contracts, `service-automation` and docs, and no `packages/cli` path. The PR's CI runs on the merge ref.
- **No out-of-scope finding filed.** `os secret orphans --delete` writes and reads back its export before deleting, which is the safe order. No other `os migrate` subcommand writes a report file after a destructive step.
